questions.text:
Let [latex]f(n)=n[/latex] and [latex]g(n)=n^{1+sin \; n}[/latex] where n is a positive integer. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. [latex]f(n)=O(g(n)) [/latex]
II. [latex]f(n)= \Omega (g(n))[/latex]
questions.solution:
[latex]g(n)=n^{1+\sin n}[/latex], and 1 + sin n keeps swinging between about 0 and 2. So g(n) is sometimes near 1 (much smaller than n) and sometimes near [latex]n^2[/latex] (much larger).

Neither bound holds for all large n.

Answer: Neither I nor II

questions.text:
Consider the equality [latex]\sum_{i=0}^{n}i^{3}=X[/latex] and the following choices for X
I.[latex] \Theta (n^{4}) [/latex]
II. [latex] \Theta (n^{5}) [/latex]
III. [latex]O (n^{5}) [/latex]
IV. [latex] \Omega (n^{3})[/latex]
The equality above remains correct if X is replaced by
questions.solution:
[latex]\sum_{i=0}^n i^3=\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)^2=\Theta(n^4)[/latex]

A [latex]\Theta(n^4)[/latex] function is also [latex]O(n^5)[/latex] and [latex]\Omega(n^3)[/latex], but it is not [latex]\Theta(n^5)[/latex].

Answer: I or III or IV but not II

questions.solution:
For each of the n iterations:
- the j loop makes [latex]p\approx\log n[/latex]
- the k loop doubles k up to p, adding [latex]\log p\approx\log\log n[/latex] to q

q [latex]\approx n\log\log n[/latex]

Answer: [latex]n\log(\log n)[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Checking each statement:
- Outer loop: n/2 + 1 iterations
- Inner loop (j doubles): about [latex]\log n[/latex] iterations
- Each adds n/2

[latex]k\approx\frac n2\cdot\log n\cdot\frac n2=\Theta(n^2\log n)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n^2\log n)[/latex]
